contentBlocks.text: You have all the pieces of a strong persuasive argument. Today, the language and organization that ties it all together.

Linking words help your reasons flow logically: 'Furthermore,' 'In addition,' 'Most importantly,' and 'Consequently' all signal how one idea connects to the next. A persuasive piece is organized in a clear order: introduce your claim, give your strongest reasons with evidence, address a counterargument, then conclude by restating your position with new energy. Take everything you've written this week — your claim, reasons, evidence, and counterargument response — and arrange them in this order, adding at least two linking words.
You just organized your entire persuasive argument using proper structure and linking words. Tomorrow you'll write the complete, finished piece.

objectives: Use linking words to connect reasons logically (furthermore, in addition, most importantly, consequently)
Organize a persuasive piece in the correct order: claim, reasons/evidence, counterargument, conclusion
materialsNeeded: All of this week's earlier worksheets
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review all the pieces built so far this week.
2. Introduce the 4 linking words and the correct organizational order.
3. Have the child arrange their own pieces in order, inserting at least 2 linking words.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow: writing the complete, finished persuasive piece.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide the organizational order as a numbered outline template to fill in rather than starting from a blank page
Ready for more: challenge them to use a different linking word than the 4 given, if they know one
This lesson is mostly reorganization of existing work, not new content creation — reassure the child that the hard thinking is already done
teacherGuide.answerKey: Answers will vary based on the child's own persuasive piece — check that the order follows claim → reasons/evidence → counterargument/response → conclusion, and that at least 2 linking words are used correctly.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Addresses Common Core Grade 5 Writing standard W.5.1c (link opinion and reasons using words and phrases), the organizational skill that ties together the whole week's argument-building work.

generationData.instructions: List your pieces in order: claim, reason 1 + evidence, reason 2 + evidence, counterargument + response. Use at least 2 linking words.
